messages:
sophia: FYI bringing up Gemma-v2 and Mistral-7B on the same serving pool. Getting a consistent quality dip after ~1k tokens when we route Mistral-tokenized requests to Gemma weights. Feels like a rotary/positional mismatch rather than vocab.
mike: Can you paste a tiny repro and the config you used? :eyes:
sophia: Minimal repro below (on dev cluster):
```
# load model variant: gemma-v2 (float16)
serve --model gemma-v2 --tokenizer mistral-tokenizer --rotary-scaling auto --rotary-base 10000
# request: long-context prompt (~1400 tokens)
```
Observed: initially OK, then sudden repetition and token collapse around 1k-1.2k.
raj: Do you see differences if you force rotary_scaling=false vs true? The implementations between Gemma forks and Mistral sometimes differ (xpos vs scaled-rope).
sophia: Yes — quick A/B:
- rotary_scaling=true -> perplexity on eval-300-long: 11.9
- rotary_scaling=false -> perplexity: 14.1 (worse)
- using Gemma tokenizer with gemma weights -> perplexity: 12.3
So when mixing Mistral tokenizer + Gemma weights, enable scaling improves but still worse than native pair.
jin: Hmm. Could be token index offsets from the tokenizer relative to rotary sin/cos frequency bins. Did you check token ids for a couple long tokens near the cutoff? Maybe vocab mapping pushes high ids and changes the effective positions.
sophia: Good point. I diffed token ids for the same text: some rare unicode sequences map to different lengths which shifts subsequent positions. Example: emoji+zwj cluster tokenized as one in Gemma but two in Mistral -> position drift.
mike: That explains drift accumulation. Two quick experiments to confirm: 1) canonicalize tokenization (force gemma tok) and route; 2) apply position reset when tokenizer mismatch detected (hacky). Which did you try?
sophia: Tried 1) — quality matched gemma baseline. For 2) I implemented a positional-offset patch (subtract cumulative token delta on each sequence) and it mitigated collapse in many cases but not all.
raj: Could also try aligning rotary base/scale. Classic mismatch: Gemma uses scaling factor of sqrt(10000) variant? Check model config: `rotary_emb.base` and `rotary_emb.xpos_scale`.
sophia: Model configs: gemma config: `rotary_emb: { base: 10000, scale: 1.0 }`
mistral config: `rotary_emb: { base: 10000, scale: 1.122 }`
So there is a small scale diff.
jin: That 12% can accumulate over long contexts. If tokens shift by even a single index the phase of sin/cos rotates differently across layers.
eval-bot: Quick stats from the last 200 long examples: mixing tokenizer+gemma weights -> exact-match drops 7.8%, repetition rate increases 2.4x.
sophia: On quantization note, q4_0 vs q8_0: q4_0 amplifies the collapse when tokenizer mismatch exists. q8_0 smoother but slightly higher latency. So quantization interacts with rotary noise.
mike: Next steps proposal:
- raj: run systematic sweep of `rotary_scale` in [0.9,1.0,1.1,1.12,1.2] for gemma weights with mistral tokenizer on 1k-long eval set.
- jin: instrument token-id drift counts per batch and produce a small histogram.
- sophia: try normalizing token ids by remapping rare clusters to canonical gemma mapping and measure.
raj: I'll kick off the sweep now and attach results to this thread.
sophia: Thanks — if sweep shows a stable compensating scale we can add a lightweight `rotary_compat` inference flag that auto-scales when tokenizer!=model-tokenizer.
mike: Agreed. If we add that, we should also include a warning in Console and an automated evaluation that triggers for long-context routes. Less surprises for customers.
sophia: I'll open a PR sketch for `rotary_compat` and include unit tests + a small quantization regression test. Assigning to @raj for numeric sweep and @jin for token-drift job. :thumbsup:
raj: got it. starting now. will post CSV when done.
